newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat dismisses Netanyahu's talk on settlements.
newsitem.headline: Arafat dismisses Netanyahu's talk on settlements.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat dismissed on Tuesday remarks by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Jewish settlement building in Arab East Jerusalem, saying the Israeli leader talked too much.
"He (is) used to speak too much," Arafat, speaking in English, told reporters in Gaza.

Arafat was referring to a statement on Sunday by Netanyahu that a corruption scandal, now apparently behind him, was motivated in part by a refusal of opposition members to accept his decision to build in Arab East Jerusalem.

"They refuse to accept the fact that the people voted for us and not for them. They refuse to accept the fact that we are building on Har Homa, they refuse to accept our efforts to protect the unity of Jerusalem...," Netanyahu said.
Arafat reiterated that Jewish settlement building at the site called Har Homa in Hebrew and Jabal Abu Ghneim in Arabic went against peace agreements and said that the Palestinians would prevent it.
"We have all the capabilities to prevent him (Netanyahu)," Arafat said without elaborating.

Israeli prosecutors announced on Sunday they would not charge Netanyahu in an influence-peddling scandal for lack of evidence. Police had recommended that Netanyahu be indicted over the short-lived appointment of an attorney-general.
The scandal cast a shadow over Middle East peacemaking, already in crisis since Netanyahu broke ground on Har Homa last month and sparked an outburst of violence.
